The client arrived settled and started work without the usual negotiation at the door.

The behavior technician ran Discrete Trial Training (DTT) on money identification with a three-item array: one, five and ten dollar bills. Prompting began at full physical. By the sixth trial he was orienting to the correct bill before the prompt arrived, so it faded to a gesture. Eight of twelve trials were correct, the last four of them independent. At snack the program shifted to Natural Environment Teaching (NET), targeting requests on his Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) device, where five unprompted mands came across the period. Tacting colors did not run. Time ran out first.

A first-then board went out before each demand, and he chose the reinforcer rather than being handed one. Two minutes of warning preceded the move to table work, with a visual timer in his line of sight. Refusals dropped sharply against last session. The timer is what changed.

Elopement from the table happened twice, both during the money program. Each was blocked, and a gestural prompt brought him back. No self-injury. A loud vocal protest came once at the transition, went unattended, and stopped after about twenty seconds.

The caregiver joined at the end and asked how the AAC device should be used at home.
